newsitem.title: UK: Halifax share rally drives valuation skyward. [CORRECTED 12:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Halifax share rally drives valuation skyward. [CORRECTED 12:25 GMT]

text.p: Halifax plc's roaring stock market debut on Monday has driven its shares to the top of the British banking league in terms of financial valuations after strong buying granted the company a 'spectacular' welcome.
At the 1115 GMT price of 7.45 stg the Halifax is trading on a prospective price/earnings multiple of over 17 times, based on BZW's 1997 earnings per share estimate of 43.2 pence.

This would rank it above even the best performing British banks, with Lloyds trading on a prospective p/e just above 16 times, trailed by HSBC on 15 times, according to data collected from Reuters 3000.
Analysts had forecast that institutional demand would force the price higher as they scrambled to pick up stock, but said this morning's rally had been breathtaking.
"This has turned into a fairly spectacular morning," said BZW analyst Timothy Sykes after turnover in Halifax stock topped 600 million (Corrects from 60 million), easily dominating the London bourse.

Institutional investors who track the FTSE-100 must build up holdings in the new bank from scratch in order to balance their portfolios to reflect Halifax's position as the eigth largest firm in the index.
Analysts said Halifax's financial fundamentals paint a bright future, but there was concern that this morning's demand was pushing the shares too far too fast.

"At these levels the shares are trading above fundamentals," said BZW's Sykes. He had previously forecast a fair-value range of 5.99 to 6.44 stg, but had told clients they should expect strong demand to drive the stock higher.

Halifax earlier said that bids to purchase stock from a central auction arranged by Halifax for new shareholders who wanted to sell immediately had ranged to as high as 8.15 stg per share and averaged 7.325 stg.
